test_title: PYST 19: SSC MTS 2024 - General Awareness (Held On: 16 Oct, 2024 - Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: From which of the following countries was the concept of the Fundamental Duties borrowed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Russia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the **Constitution of Russia (formerly USSR)**.
 
• These duties were added by the **42nd Amendment Act** in 1976 during the Emergency period in India.
 
• Initially, there were **ten Fundamental Duties** listed in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• An additional duty was added by the **86th Amendment Act** in 2002, making the total number of Fundamental Duties eleven.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act**

 
 
• Also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its comprehensive scope.
 
• Enacted in 1976 during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• Introduced significant changes, including the addition of Fundamental Duties and changes to the Preamble.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• Article 51A of the Indian Constitution lists Fundamental Duties for every citizen.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens about their moral obligations to uphold the spirit of patriotism and to support the unity of India.
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, these duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act**
 
 
• Enacted in 2002, this amendment made education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Article 21A was introduced, and the Right to Education became a constitutional guarantee.
 
• An additional Fundamental Duty was introduced for parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children.
